source.title: Beyond Components: Singular Vector-Based Interpretability of Transformer Circuits
source.authors: Areeb Ahmad; Abhinav Joshi; Ashutosh Modi

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some passages contain apparent wording or consistency errors, but the text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies a different, direction-level masking method to GPT-2 Small IOI and reports how well the masked model preserves IOI behavior, as well as how learned directions align with previously identified IOI heads.
record.gate_note: The study does not ablate everything outside the 26-head circuit or patch heads to test their stated causal roles. Its IOI mask results and analyses of named circuit heads/directions are included; cited results from prior work and comparisons to SVD baselines are not treated as new results about the original circuit.
record.test_reason: The study learns sparse SVD-direction masks for GPT-2 small on IOI, a circuit-finding method different from the original. It reports, mainly in figures and text, that heads in Wang et al.'s circuit get higher mask values than other heads. That bears on V4. Its accuracy and KL numbers describe its own masked model, not the original 26-head circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that GPT-2 components multiplex several low-rank subfunctions along singular directions, so computation is more distributed than head-level circuits assume. They also say that high mask values on Wang et al.'s circuit heads give quantitative validation of the prior IOI circuit. They concede the method does not establish end-to-end causal mediation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SVD decomposition and optimized direction masks to reconstruct model outputs, rather than the original circuit discovery, head ablation, and activation-patching tests.

fits_no_version.finding: Named IOI heads (9.6, 9.9, 10.0) each contain several distinct low-rank QK directions: sequence start, entity/action separation, entity salience, and inhibition of repeated names.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuit heads are not monolithic; their functions decompose into separable singular directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse direction masks (about 9% of directions kept) reproduce IOI behaviour with KL 0.21 and accuracy 0.70 vs 0.79 for the full model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI behaviour in GPT-2 small can be reconstructed from a small set of singular directions, including MLP directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Some directions of head 9.6 (S1, S7) show the same pattern in IOI, GP and GT prompts, shown on example instances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sub-head directions are reused across tasks.

record.problems: The IOI evidence is limited to GPT-2 Small and a direction-mask reconstruction objective. The paper does not directly test the original circuit's outside-circuit ablation or patching criteria, and it notes that direction-level interpretability does not by itself establish end-to-end causal mediation.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable reported IOI results were omitted. Results for Gender Pronoun interventions and Greater Than numerical reasoning were not included because they do not test the IOI claim versions.

untested.parts: The faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the 26-head circuit, and the head roles tested by patching, are not tested.
Backup takeover after name-mover ablation is not tested.
Other models, sizes and checkpoints are not tested, and IOI head classes are not shown reused in other tasks.
There is no quantitative overlap with the original circuit, no other ablation types or metrics, and no check on the early-layer classes (previous-token, duplicate-token, induction).
No variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution for the original circuit.
Name orders, templates and more names are not tested.

missing.what: Average QK mask value by Wang et al. head class compared with other heads. Circuit heads, especially the name mover classes, are reported as higher; no numbers are given.
missing.locator: Figure 7; Section 4 text on Figures 1 and 5

missing.what: Statement that components not associated with known circuits get near-zero masks.

record.verdict_notes: I relinked all rows to none. R1–R4 describe the study's own method, and R5–R13 are sub-head direction properties, not head-level roles. The only bearing on a version is the figure-level agreement with the circuit heads, which bears on V4 and has no row. V4 is marked not_tested in the record; I treat it as tested qualitatively. The masks were trained with Bhaskar et al.'s corrupted IOI data.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the exact 26-head, 7-class circuit by removing everything outside it, nor does it test all stated head roles by patching. It does not evaluate the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
No ablation of main name-mover heads followed by a test of backup-head takeover is reported.

The cross-task direction-role observations concern GPT-2 Small only. The study does not test the same IOI circuit in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or show that the full head classes and roles carry IOI there.
No comparison of circuit recovery across other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics is reported.
The study reports reconstruction fidelity and task performance under directional masking, but does not vary ablation type, metric, or IOI prompt distribution to test their sensitivity.
No systematic evaluation across IOI name orders, templates, or prompts with more names is reported.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Learned sparse SVD-direction masks were used to prune directions while reconstructing model outputs.
rows.note: This is the study's learned direction-level sparsity, not a test of the original 26-head circuit's completeness.
rows.check: Sparsity of the study's own learned direction mask is a property of its method, not of the original circuit. It is not a V1 or V5 measurement.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: IOI model behavior was reconstructed using learned sparse SVD-direction masks.
rows.measure: KL divergence between original and masked model predictive distributions
rows.baseline: Original model predictive distribution; numeric baseline not stated
rows.note: The reported reconstruction is not exact; the study describes it as high-fidelity.
rows.check: KL 0.21 is the faithfulness of the study's own masked model. It says nothing about the original circuit's faithfulness or about how sensitive that circuit's evaluation is (V5).

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: IOI model behavior was reconstructed using learned sparse SVD-direction masks.
rows.measure: Task accuracy, pruned versus full model
rows.note: The pruned model retains substantial task accuracy but is below the full model as reported.
rows.check: Pruned 0.70 vs full 0.79 accuracy is the study's own method's performance, not a test of the 26-head circuit.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: IOI model behavior was reconstructed using learned sparse SVD-direction masks.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the masked-model exact match; it does not provide a full-model exact-match comparator in the table.
rows.check: Exact match 0.77 belongs to the study's own masked model. No comparator bears on any version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Learned SVD-direction mask value for S1, interpreted as sequence-initialization detection.
rows.note: The mask value measures learned retention, not a patching effect.
rows.check: A mask value for one QK direction of head 9.6 does not measure the head's IOI role named in V1.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Learned SVD-direction mask value for S7, interpreted as separating entities from actions.
rows.note: The mask value does not establish the direction's causal role under patching.
rows.check: Same as R5: a direction-level mask value with a role defined by this study.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Learned SVD-direction mask value for S28, interpreted as entity salience and detection.
rows.note: The mask value does not establish the direction's causal role under patching.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed S7 attention scores for entity and action token categories.
rows.note: This is a directional score contrast, not a causal patching test.
rows.check: The entity-vs-action score contrast is a new sub-head function, not one of the V1 head roles.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed S28 activations by token category.
rows.note: The table lists example activation values, not a causal intervention.
rows.check: These are example activations only, for a sub-head entity-salience direction.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 9 (Head 9.9)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the unnormalized attention score for repeated entity mentions with initial mentions along S16.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as an inhibitory pattern; they do not patch the direction to test IOI performance.
rows.check: One QK direction of name mover 9.9 scores repeated names 2.31 lower. This is suggestive of the name-mover role but is not a head-level or causal measure.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 10 Head 0 (Head 10.0)
rows.operation_detail: Measured how often S20 assigned higher attention to the indirect-object token.
rows.measure: Cases in which the indirect object received higher attention
rows.note: The paper describes this as a partial bias; this is not a causal test of the direction's contribution to IOI accuracy.
rows.check: A single direction of head 10.0 favours the IO in about 54–59% of cases. This does not measure the head's role.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Examined S1 attention patterns as a start-of-sequence detector across task contexts.
rows.value: The text states that S1 consistently detects the start of the sequence across task contexts.
rows.note: Cross-task role reuse is reported for this direction in GPT-2 Small; it does not test transfer of the IOI circuit to other models.
rows.check: Cross-task reuse is shown for a generic start-of-sequence direction from one instance figure. It is not an IOI head class or role reused in another task.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small, Layer 9 Head 6 (Head 9.6)
rows.operation_detail: Examined S7 attention patterns as an entity-action separator across task contexts.
rows.value: The text states that S7 consistently separates entity/object tokens from actions across contexts.
rows.note: Cross-task role reuse is reported for this direction in GPT-2 Small; it does not test transfer of the IOI circuit to other models.
rows.check: The entity/action separator is a role defined by this study, shown on single example prompts. It is not V3's IOI head classes carrying another task.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small IOI, direction-mask method; late-layer name mover, backup and negative name mover heads
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Fig. 1, 5, 7), no row: these circuit heads show higher average mask values than other heads. Non-circuit heads show near-zero masks. The evidence is qualitative only.
relationships.display_finding: Name mover, backup, and negative name mover heads had higher average masks than other heads, while non-circuit heads had near-zero masks.

relation.reason: Section 4 and Figures 1, 5 and 7 report correspondence between learned direction masks and previously identified IOI heads, directly bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: SVD direction masking provides a different circuit-discovery method and compares its selected components with the established GPT-2 small IOI circuit.
